script: The second snow hits the ground, some dogs turn into complete maniacs, zooming, face-planting, digging like there's treasure buried underneath. Part of it is pure novelty, snow is a totally new texture and resistance under their paws, and dogs are wired to investigate anything unfamiliar with their whole body. Part of it is ancestry, plenty of breeds descend from dogs built for cold climates, so snow triggers old instincts tied to hunting and moving through winter terrain. There's also a cooling factor, dogs don't sweat the way we do, so for a dog that runs hot, snow feels genuinely relieving against the skin. And the crunch and push-back of snow under their paws mimics the resistance of chasing something, which flips on that same playful predatory drive. So that snow-zoomie chaos isn't randomness, it's a full sensory reset button. Want more real dog behavior insight? The link's below.
